caption: A leading space stays inside the active math guard.
eval:
(async () => { const p = app.plugins.plugins['steady-inline-math']; p.settings.enabled = true; p.pro.signOut(); const leaf = app.workspace.getMostRecentLeaf(); const s = leaf.getViewState(); await leaf.setViewState({ ...s, state: { ...s.state, mode: 'source', source: false } }); const v = [...p.guard.views].find(v => p.filePath(v.state) === app.workspace.getActiveFile()?.path); if (!v) throw new Error('No editor'); p.settings.enabled = false; v.dispatch({ changes: { from: 0, to: v.state.doc.length, insert: "# Math practice

Use one caret in a plain paragraph. Put it just inside a dollar sign, type a space, then move it into the text.

The first result is $x+y$. Keep the equation active while you add a space before x.

The second result is $E=mc^2$. Add a space after the last term, then leave the equation.

## Braces that I wrote

This source includes my empty braces: $x{}+y$. The guard must keep them when I leave.

## After the edit

My text is kept when the temporary guard leaves. Undo and Redo apply to the space that I type.

The sample uses plain paragraphs. Headings, code and tables are outside the guard scope.
" }, selection: { anchor: 0 }, annotations: [] }); p.settings.enabled = true; v.focus(); const at = v.state.doc.toString().indexOf("$x+y$") + 1; if (at < 1) throw new Error('Missing equation'); v.dispatch({ selection: { anchor: at } }); const pos = v.state.selection.main.head; v.dispatch({ changes: { from: pos, insert: ' ' }, selection: { anchor: pos + 1 }, userEvent: 'input.type' }); return 'ok'; })()
